title: A Model of Chronic Pain
summary:
Body pain helps humans recognize dangers in the environment. Pain is therefore important for us to avoid such dangers. However, there are also many people who suffer from pain that sometimes lasts for years without any good reason. It is not yet clearly understood why pain persists despite the absence of an immediate cause. Currently, it is believed that the transition to persistent pain is signaled very early by the body during an acute pain response.

In this study, we will test a model of long-lasting pain. The aim is to investigate how the transition to chronic pain can be influenced by various tasks.

All participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups, each of which will perform different tasks in the experiment. In all groups, participants will be repeatedly exposed to pressure and heat pain stimuli, partly while brain activity and brain anatomy are recorded using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and partly during the execution of one of the tasks. The data analysis will compare pain perception and brain scans between the groups.
conditions: In an experimental model, the influence of cognitive performance and physical activity on the development of chronic pain is being investigated.

interventions.name: Arm 1: Experimental cognitive performance intervention (5 sessions of 45 minutes each on 5 consecutive days)
Arm 2: Experimental physical performance intervention (5 sessions of 45 minutes each on 5 consecutive days)
Arm 3: Control condition (5 sessions of 45 minutes each on 5 consecutive days)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy adult participants, male and female, who are fully capable of making decisions and able to understand the informed consent, and who are able to reliably perform the stimulus assessments.

Body Mass Index: 18 to 30
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute or chronic pain (including muscle soreness)
- Presence of acute or chronic somatic or psychiatric conditions (based on self-report or routine examination)
- Presence of MRI-specific exclusion criteria (claustrophobia, pacemakers, non-MRI-compatible metallic implants)
- Participation in studies involving medication or regular medication intake (except thyroid medication, allergy medication, occasional use of painkillers, or contraceptives)
- Use of painkillers within the last 24 hours before the examination
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Acute skin condition or injury at the stimulation sites
- Acute respiratory illness or symptoms
- No past or current physical opioid dependence
- No cardiovascular diseases
- No nervous system disorders
- No immune system disorders
- No gastrointestinal diseases
- No use of cardiotoxic medications/substances (e.g., cocaine, methamphetamine, cyclic antidepressants, calcium channel blockers, beta-blockers, digoxin)
